❓ Entrada / Instrucción Multimodal:
Please generate a comprehensive and professional pathology report based on the provided slide from Adrenal gland, including key elements such as: (1) the histopathological diagnosis, (2) tumor morphology and growth patterns, (3) extent of invasion and involved structures, (4) lymphovascular or perineural invasion, (5) status of surgical margins, (6) TNM staging if possible, and (7) any additional pathological findings including non-neoplastic tissue alterations.
🎯 Respuesta Patológica de Referencia (Ground Truth):
The pathological examination reveals an adrenocortical carcinoma following the resection of a large adrenal mass and the left kidney. The tumor is characterized by a significant size and a heterogeneous appearance with multilobulated yellow areas and necrosis involving approximately 20% of the mass. This carcinoma demonstrates a high nuclear grade (Fuhrman 4) and a diffuse architectural pattern, with clear cells comprising less than a quarter of the tumor. The mitotic activity is high, with 28 mitoses per 10 high-power fields, including the presence of atypical mitoses. Notably, the tumor presents with capsular and venous invasion, while sinusoidal invasion is absent, contributing to a WEISS score of 8, indicating aggressive behavior. The renal parenchyma appears unaffected by neoplastic infiltration, and the surgical margins, marked with green Indian ink, are critical for assessing the completeness of resection. Although the ureter is somewhat dilated, no other macroscopic changes are noted in the displaced left kidney adjacent to the mass. There is no mention of lymph node involvement in the specimen provided.

❓ Entrada / Instrucción Multimodal:
Please generate a comprehensive and professional pathology report based on the provided slide from Bladder, including key elements such as: (1) the histopathological diagnosis, (2) tumor morphology and growth patterns, (3) extent of invasion and involved structures, (4) lymphovascular or perineural invasion, (5) status of surgical margins, (6) TNM staging if possible, and (7) any additional pathological findings including non-neoplastic tissue alterations.
🎯 Respuesta Patológica de Referencia (Ground Truth):
The essential pathological findings indicate a diagnosis of high-grade invasive urothelial carcinoma, primarily involving the bladder, with confirmed growth patterns of both papillary and flat for the non-invasive component. The invasive component exhibits inverted/nodular growth and is identified as multicentric. Local invasion is limited to the superficial half of the muscularis propria, and there is no extravesical extension or involvement of the ureters and urethra. Both vascular and perineural invasions are absent, and surgical margins are free of tumor. The prostate shows nodular hyperplasia and small foci of adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 6, confined to the prostate without seminal vesicle or bladder neck involvement. Lymph node dissections from the right pelvic, retroperitoneal, and left pelvic areas reveal no involvement, and biopsies from the vas deferens, ureters, periureteral tissue, and urachus are benign. Overall, the pathological stage is pT2a for the bladder carcinoma and pT2b for the prostate adenocarcinoma.

❓ Entrada / Instrucción Multimodal:
Please generate a comprehensive and professional pathology report based on the provided slide from Breast, including key elements such as: (1) the histopathological diagnosis, (2) tumor morphology and growth patterns, (3) extent of invasion and involved structures, (4) lymphovascular or perineural invasion, (5) status of surgical margins, (6) TNM staging if possible, and (7) any additional pathological findings including non-neoplastic tissue alterations.
🎯 Respuesta Patológica de Referencia (Ground Truth):
The patient was diagnosed with a left breast invasive ductal carcinoma, which was addressed through a segmental mastectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy. Pathological examination revealed a high-grade (Nottingham Grade III) invasive ductal carcinoma, measuring 2.6 cm in its largest dimension. The carcinoma was positive for Estrogen Receptors (H-score: 250), Progesterone Receptors (H-score: 75), and HER2. Additionally, ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) of nuclear grade 3, solid type with comedo necrosis, was present and constituted 40% of the total tumor volume, intermingled with the invasive component. Importantly, no lymphovascular space invasion was noted, and all resection margins were free of carcinoma, with the invasive component and DCIS being 0.4 cm and 0.3 cm from the nearest (anterior) margin, respectively. The surgical margins closest to the tumor were 4 mm for the invasive component and 3 mm for the DCIS. All four lymph nodes examined, including sentinel and non-sentinel nodes, were negative for metastatic carcinoma. The non-neoplastic breast tissue exhibited various benign changes, including ductal epithelial hyperplasia, intraductal papilloma, radial scar, columnar cell changes, and fibrocystic changes, alongside previous biopsy site alterations. The pathological staging classified the tumor as pT2 pNO (sn), indicating a primary tumor larger than 2 cm but not more than 5 cm, with no regional lymph node metastasis.

🎯 Respuesta Patológica de Referencia (Ground Truth):
The pathological findings reveal a diagnosis of moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, exhibiting mixed growth patterns, including acinar, papillary, and micropapillary. The tumor shows angiolymphatic invasion, yet no visceral pleural invasion is observed. Surgical parenchymal margins are free of carcinoma, indicating complete excision. Lymph node dissections from stations #6, #7, #9, and #10L yield a total of ten nodes, all of which are negative for metastatic carcinoma, suggesting no regional lymph node involvement. Additionally, some nodes display partial calcification and fibrosis without malignancy. The immunohistochemical profile, with CK7 and TTF1 positivity, supports a lung primary origin for the adenocarcinoma. The left upper lobe also exhibits bullous emphysematous changes but remains free of carcinoma in other submitted sections.

Please generate a comprehensive and professional pathology report based on the provided slide from Kidney, including key elements such as: (1) the histopathological diagnosis, (2) tumor morphology and growth patterns, (3) extent of invasion and involved structures, (4) lymphovascular or perineural invasion, (5) status of surgical margins, (6) TNM staging if possible, and (7) any additional pathological findings including non-neoplastic tissue alterations.
🎯 Respuesta Patológica de Referencia (Ground Truth):
The pathological examination reveals distinct findings in the right kidney allograft and the right native kidney. The allograft kidney demonstrates severe chronic allograft nephropathy characterized by calcific graft atherosclerosis and mild to moderate acute rejection with associated lymphoid hyperplasia. The native kidney contains a renal cell carcinoma of granular and clear cell type, identified as Fuhrman's nuclear grade III. This tumor exhibits focal involvement of the pelvi-calyceal system; however, it is surgically resected with negative margins and shows no evidence of vascular invasion. The pathological stage is classified as T1, with the nodal and metastatic status not assessed (NX, MX), and graded as G3. Additionally, a separate low-grade renal cell neoplasm with focal papillary architecture is present, as well as multiple cysts with focal hemorrhage indicative of end-stage renal disease. No lymph node involvement is documented in either of the renal pathology findings.

❓ Entrada / Instrucción Multimodal:
Construct a brief narrative that clearly summarizes the essential findings of the pathology analysis from the whole slide image.
🎯 Respuesta Patológica de Referencia (Ground Truth):
The specimen analysis reveals a diagnosis of invasive high-grade urothelial carcinoma on radical cystoprostatectomy involving the bladder and prostate. The tumor is noted to invade the muscularis propria, with urothelial carcinoma in situ identified in both the bladder and the prostatic urethra. Margins of the urethra and surrounding soft tissue are negative for tumor involvement, although the right ureter margin is positive for urothelial carcinoma in situ. The prostate displays benign prostatic hyperplasia with no malignant involvement in the prostate parenchyma. Examination of the pelvic lymph nodes from two separate excisions shows no lymph node involvement, with fifteen nodes from the first group and three from the second group all negative for neoplasm. The pathological staging is classified as pT2a pNO pMX, indicating the tumor invades the superficial muscularis propria, no regional lymph node metastasis is present, and distant metastasis cannot be assessed. There is no evidence of venous lymphatic invasion, and in total, nineteen lymph nodes were examined with none found to be involved by the tumor. The findings collectively point towards a locally invasive urothelial carcinoma without regional or distant spread, though with significant in situ involvement necessitating thorough clinical management.

❓ Entrada / Instrucción Multimodal:
How does hormone replacement therapy affect the risk of developing invasive ductal carcinoma?
🎯 Respuesta Patológica de Referencia (Ground Truth):
Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is associated with an increased risk of developing invasive ductal carcinoma, which is the most common type of breast cancer. This risk is particularly linked to combined estrogen-progestin therapy, rather than estrogen alone. The use of HRT may stimulate the growth of breast cells, leading to an increased risk of mutations and cancer development. Studies have shown that women who take combined HRT for several years have a higher risk of developing invasive breast cancer than those who have never used the therapy. Importantly, once the use of HRT is discontinued, the increased risk diminishes over time. In the context of managing menopause symptoms, the decision to use HRT should be made after careful consideration of the benefits and risks, in consultation with a healthcare provider.
